title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 439 (Offences to be non-cognizable)

content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 439 (Offences to be non-cognizable). Every offence under the Act is deemed non-cognizable, except the offences the section excepts. The section applies only to the persons, companies, and transactions it names. A filing, approval, or penalty arises only where the section or a rule under it says so. It does not create a power that is reserved to another section or to the Tribunal. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: Explanation
sections.body: A court takes cognizance only on a complaint by the Registrar, a shareholder or a person authorised by the Central Government, as the section states. Fraud under section 447 is within the exception the section makes.
